info.title: Vendor Service - Multi-Vendor Consolidation and Mission Planning
info.description:
Fulfilment planning with a customer-chosen delivery preference, and the alternatives the optimizer considered.

A plan is now one candidate among several rather than the only answer there is. Every alternative the optimizer could construct is built, priced through the real logistics authorities, compared under the customer's chosen mode, and kept with the reason it won or lost. That is what makes the questions Support actually receives answerable: why two vendors were combined, why the order was split, why FASTEST cost more, and why SAVER could not combine two pickups.

THE FULFILMENT PREFERENCE is the one value a customer may contribute to planning, and it is safe for a structural reason rather than a hopeful one: it CHOOSES among alternatives the server built and the authorities priced. It can no more set a fee than it can set a distance.

THE LIVE MULTI-STOP LIMITATION. Neither driver-dispatch-delivery-service nor driver-hauling-service models a mission with several separate collection points. A consolidated candidate spanning two pickup locations is therefore built, evaluated and REJECTED with MULTI_STOP_UNSUPPORTED, and the executable split alternative is planned instead. Several vendors at ONE physical pickup point - two kitchens in a food court, two traders in a market - are one stop and still consolidate normally. The capability is read from configuration, so the gate opens without a code change when a runtime gains it.

post.summary: Plan delivery for a validated checkout session
post.description:
Builds every alternative, prices each through the owning logistics authority, selects one under the requested preference, and persists all of them with their reasons.

An UNSERVICEABLE plan is returned with 200. It is a successful planning outcome that names precisely which vendors cannot be delivered and why, which is more useful than a 4xx carrying none of it.

requestBody.description: Optional. An absent or empty body means no stated preference and plans BALANCED. A body that is present but malformed is refused rather than defaulted, because silently planning BALANCED for a customer who asked for SAVER would hide a client bug behind a plausible plan.

409.description: The underlying state changed while the caller was deciding.

422.description: The request could not be understood.

get.summary: Read the current plan for a checkout session

409.description: The underlying state changed while the caller was deciding.

422.description: The request could not be understood.

customerBearer.description: Customer Service access token. The customer is taken from the verified subject claim and NEVER from a request body: no route in this document accepts a customer id, a price, a delivery fee, a vendor selection or a winning candidate as input.

fulfilment_preference.description:
FASTEST minimises time to the last delivery and may choose parallel missions even when consolidation would be cheaper. BALANCED is the default trade-off. SAVER minimises what the customer pays, inside the wider delivery window they accepted.

No mode may override a safety or service constraint. A capacity limit, a temperature rule, a fragile load, a closed handover window, a promised arrival time or a missing runtime capability refuses a consolidation in every mode, and the refusal is recorded as INELIGIBLE rather than as a price decision.

mode.description: The preference this plan was optimized for. It flows unchanged into the CheckoutQuote as selected_fulfilment_mode, so a plan quoted as SAVER cannot later be executed as FASTEST against a charge the customer never approved.

optimization_policy_version.description: The threshold envelope the comparison was decided under. Thresholds move; an explanation that silently re-read today's numbers would have stopped explaining what happened.

candidates.description: Every alternative considered, selected and rejected alike. Keeping the losers is the point: a plan that stored only the winner cannot answer why the other option was not chosen.

Funding.description: customer + vendor + platform always equals gross, enforced by the database. It is what keeps 'who actually paid for this delivery' answerable at settlement.

status.description: INELIGIBLE is not REJECTED. A candidate refused by a safety or capability constraint was never a real option, and recording it as rejected-on-price would suggest the optimizer weighed safety against money. The database refuses to store a constraint reason on any other status.

completion_minutes.description: Time to the LAST delivery. Parallel legs overlap, so this is not the sum of the legs.

detour_minutes.description: How much longer this candidate's slowest leg is than the slowest leg of the fully split alternative. Measured against the split alternative's own QUOTED transit, not against an estimate - which is why both alternatives are priced before either is compared.

service_capabilities.description: Which logistics authorities could drive a multi-stop collection at the moment of the decision. Without it, reading MULTI_STOP_UNSUPPORTED back in a year would be an assertion with nothing behind it.
